lines.text: Do you know how Bluetooth works? Your earbuds, your watch and your phone talk all day, without a single wire.
Bluetooth is radio, at two point four gigahertz. The same band as Wi-Fi, and even microwave ovens.
That band is crowded. So classic Bluetooth hops: it jumps between seventy nine channels, up to sixteen hundred times a second, and both devices hop together.
When you pair, the two devices create a shared secret key. Next time they find each other on their own, and everything they send is encrypted.
Bluetooth Low Energy, used by watches and trackers, sends tiny bursts, then sleeps. That's how a tracker battery can last a year.
Range is usually around ten meters. Walls, and even your body, soak up the signal.
Orbi needs no pairing at all. Open orbitransfer.com on phones on the same Wi-Fi, and they show up in Nearby. No login, and every file is locked before it's sent.
